# Wait for asynchronous dock drops before source cleanup

## Context

While repairing Demo B's missing proxy embodiment under #18516, the target began producing a ready preview and accepting the transfer. The source nevertheless emitted cancellation and cleaned itself up before the asynchronous target answered. The consumer ticket explicitly excludes engine changes; this is its bounded engine prerequisite.

## The Problem

At dev `335b2ca43a5ec54c823563745c276c3881e05416`, an exact-source probe of `DragCoordinator.onDragEnd` and `TabSortZone.processDragEnd`, with a deferred successful target and neutral base cleanup, records:

```text
Before target settlement:
reset → dockTearOutCancel → dockVesselConversionRetired → base-cleanup → reset
After target settlement:
remote-out
remoteDropCommitted after cleanup: true
```

The coordinator attaches a callback but does not return its promise. The dock caller therefore reads `remoteDropCommitted` before it can become true, chooses the refusal path, and may retire the converted vessel. This is independently reproduced from unchanged engine methods; it is not inferred solely from a browser timeout. The browser investigation and phase receipts are linked in the [consumer diagnosis](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18516#issuecomment-5594817229).

Historical repair #15248 / #15326 correctly made source retirement depend on the target's outcome and preserved same-stack synchronous behavior. Its documented assumption that asynchronous source cleanup has no immediate outcome reader no longer holds in the dock conversion path. This successor preserves that outcome contract and carries completion to the reader.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs:onDragEnd` owns remote target arbitration, invokes `onRemoteDrop`, and calls the source's `onRemoteDropOut` only after commitment. It remains dock-blind.
- `src/dashboard/dock/interaction/TabSortZone.mjs:processDragEnd` owns dock terminal selection in both ordinary pane and whole-stack paths.
- `src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs:onDragEnd` already holds `dragEndActive` across asynchronous processing; the dock start path already refuses while that latch is active.
- `src/core/Base.mjs` owns destruction and asynchronous cancellation through `isDestroyed` and `trap`. Destruction removes writable instance properties, so an unconditional asynchronous `finally` must not recreate them.

## The Fix

Return asynchronous target completion from the coordinator and conditionally await it at the dock terminal decision. Preserve the synchronous path on the same call stack. Use the existing source latch and Base lifecycle for pending/destroyed sources; do not introduce a second gesture tracker.

Keep coordinator arbitration cleanup synchronous. A delayed completion must not clear a later gesture's active target. Capture the source/item for the accepted call, suppress late source callbacks after destruction, and preserve target rejection. Guard the existing base latch cleanup against instance destruction.

Extend the existing manager and dock unit specs with deferred outcomes and lifecycle controls. No new module is needed.

## Contract Ledger

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DragCoordinator.onDragEnd` | Target `onRemoteDrop` outcome; existing #15248 contract | Synchronous result retires the source synchronously; asynchronous completion is returned and retires only on a committed result while source remains alive | Null/false/rejection never calls remote-out; rejection remains observable | Method JSDoc | Deferred success/null/rejection and same-stack controls in existing manager spec |
| `TabSortZone.processDragEnd`, ordinary and stack branches | Coordinator completion and source `remoteDropCommitted` | Wait before selecting the terminal or starting source cleanup when target is asynchronous | Refused/cancelled paths remain zero-remote-out; failed commit propagates after applicable cleanup | Method JSDoc | Pending state, exact-once terminal, stack and ordinary controls |
| `SortZone.onDragEnd` latch | Existing `dragEndActive` and Base destruction | Duplicate end and new dock start stay excluded while completion is pending; destroyed instances gain no late state | Destruction suppresses source callbacks and follows existing Base cancellation semantics | Existing latch JSDoc | Real Neo-instance destruction and pending-start controls |
| Coordinator active gesture state | Existing synchronous terminal cleanup | Older completion cannot erase a newer active target | No new epoch/cache or deferred global reset | Coordinator JSDoc | Interleaved-source control |

## Decision Record impact

Aligned with ADR 0029's outcome-before-source-retirement boundary. No new semantic authority or change to Group transactions, preview eligibility, or native-window policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A deferred target leaves the dock source pending: no cancellation, vessel retirement, local commit, committed terminal, or base cleanup before settlement.
- [ ] Successful settlement produces exactly one source remote-out and the committed terminal; null/false and rejected settlements produce no remote-out. Rejection remains observable.
- [ ] Ordinary and stack paths obey the same completion boundary. Existing synchronous outcomes still notify the source on the initiating call stack.
- [ ] Duplicate end/new dock start cannot overlap a pending source end. Destruction causes no late source callback, lifecycle event, or recreated instance field.
- [ ] A prior target's completion cannot clear a different source's newer coordinator state.
- [ ] Focused existing manager/dock unit suites pass with discriminating deferred controls, including a recorded failing control before the repair. The headed Demo B adoption remains acceptance work of #18516 after this prerequisite.

## Out of Scope

Demo B embodiment wiring, receipt/projection ordering and mount witnesses; broad drag architecture or cleanup refactors; new coordination state; changing target commit semantics; KB ingestion.

## Avoided Traps

- Making the coordinator unconditionally `async` moves synchronous retirement past its existing reader.
- Deferring all coordinator cleanup until settlement lets an old gesture erase a newer one.
- Increasing browser waits or mount-count allowances does not repair premature cancellation.
- Reopening the completed predecessor conflates the earlier null-outcome repair with this newly reachable completion reader.
